definitions.explanation: The entire span of a person's life from birth to death.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{生涯|しょうがい}を{音楽|おんがく}に{捧|ささ}げた。
examples.english: He devoted his whole life to music.

examples.japanese: {生涯|しょうがい}{学習|がくしゅう}は{大切|たいせつ}だ。
その{作家|さっか}は{生涯|しょうがい}で100{冊|さつ}{以上|いじょう}の{本|ほん}を{書|か}いた。{亡|な}くなった{今|いま}でも、その{作品|さくひん}は{世界中|せかいじゅう}で{読|よ}まれている。
examples.english: That author wrote over 100 books in his lifetime. Even now after his death, his works are read around the world.

notes:
{生涯|しょうがい} refers to one's entire lifetime - the whole span of life.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {生涯|しょうがい}を{通|つう}じて (throughout one's life)
- {生涯|しょうがい}を{捧|ささ}げる (to devote one's life to)
- {生涯|しょうがい}にわたって (throughout one's lifetime)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {生涯|しょうがい}{学習|がくしゅう} (lifelong learning)
- {生涯|しょうがい}{賃金|ちんぎん} (lifetime earnings)
- {生涯|しょうがい}{独身|どくしん} (lifelong bachelor/bachelorette)
- {生涯|しょうがい}{現役|げんえき} (active until the end of life)
- {生涯|しょうがい}スポーツ (lifetime sports)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {生涯|しょうがい}: lifetime (emphasis on the whole span)
- {一生|いっしょう}: whole life (similar meaning, slightly more casual)
- {人生|じんせい}: life (broader concept, life journey)

NOTE: {生涯|しょうがい} and {障害|しょうがい} (obstacle/disability) are homophones.
